sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and project header
sections.what: Brings in the built-in tools for running commands, reading and writing files, and generating a random secret. The header explains the job: prepare Node, packages, the environment file, the database, migrations and seed data.
sections.why: The header and the imports show the script needs these built-in tools for its steps.
sections.watch_out: The header says some steps need scripts that do not exist yet, so an early run prints TODO messages rather than failing.

sections.name: sh
sections.title: Command runner and Node version check
sections.what: Defines a helper that prints each command and runs it, stopping the script if the command fails. It checks that Node.js is at least 20.9, installs packages with npm ci when a lock file exists or npm install otherwise, and creates a local settings file with a new secret if none exists.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app needs a recent Node version, and a lock file gives repeatable installs. The error message names the Next.js version as the reason for the version limit.
sections.watch_out: The success message about the new secret prints even if the example file has no secret line to replace, so the secret may never be written.

sections.name: todo
sections.title: Database steps and TODO list
sections.what: Runs the database npm scripts for starting the database, migrating its layout and seeding sample data, when each exists in package.json. Missing scripts go onto a TODO list printed at the end, and the Prisma client is generated when appropriate. Then it prints that initialisation is complete.
sections.why: Likely reason: the database steps depend on scripts not yet created, so the setup can run early and report what is still missing.
sections.watch_out: The completion message prints even when TODO items remain, so a clean-looking finish does not mean the database is ready.

summary: A setup script that gets a fresh copy of the project ready to run: it checks Node.js, installs packages, creates a local settings file with a new secret, and runs database steps when their scripts exist.
purpose: Saves the owner from running setup steps by hand, and shows which steps are still missing.
why: The header states the job is to bootstrap the project and to report steps not yet built as TODO. Likely reason for the generated secret: a login secret should be private and unique to each copy.
how: Stops if Node.js is older than 20.9. Runs npm ci when a lock file exists, otherwise npm install. If no local settings file exists, copies the example file and inserts a random secret. Runs the database up, migrate and seed npm scripts if they exist, otherwise records them as TODO. Generates the Prisma client when no migrate script exists but a Prisma schema does. Prints the TODO list and a completion message.
inputs: package.json, the optional package-lock.json, the example settings file, the local settings file if it exists, and prisma/schema.prisma if present. Node.js and npm must be installed, and the script must run from the project's top folder.
outputs: Installed packages, a local settings file with a secret if it was missing, database changes made by the npm scripts, and printed messages.
risks: If the example settings file has no secret line, the script still reports that a secret was created. Any failing step stops the whole script, so later steps do not run. The settings file holds a secret that must never be committed.
debug: Node too old: install the current LTS version. Install failure: read the npm output above the error. Secret missing: check the example file for the secret line. TODO items: create the named npm scripts. Path errors: run the script from the project root.
